clue.text: Gibraltar resident in pub repeatedly getting to talk with energy

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word for a pub is written down twice in a row

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to yap is to talk, chatter
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone from Gibraltar sits in the pub chatting energetically, round after round.
explanation.walkthrough: The Barbary apes (macaques) living on the Rock of Gibraltar are its most famous residents; 'resident' tempts you to think of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barbary macaque colony on the Rock is the only wild monkey population in Europe, so these animals are literally local inhabitants.

clue.text: Champagne makes one animated

definitions.meaning: sparkling wine, informally called by a fizzy nickname
lively and full of high spirits

explanation.surface: A glass of champagne gets anyone going.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both slang for sparkling wine and an adjective for a lively, effervescent personality.

clue.text: Stirs up French author tearing out first page, then second

indicators.note: tearing out says a letter is ripped away from the author's name, like a page from a book

parts.note: Marcel Proust wrote In Search of Lost Time

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word page

explanation.surface: A vandal rips the first page from a Proust volume, then the next one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tearing out' removes P (first of 'page') from PROUST, leaving ROUST; 'second' is S, not another page.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to rouse or drive someone out, so the plural verb matches stirs up.

clue.text: A male deep-toned with a robe suitable for diplomat

parts.note: a bass voice or instrument is deep-toned
a dress is a robe, a gown

explanation.surface: A man with a deep voice wears a gown fit for an embassy function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suitable for' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a woman serving as an envoy, a female member of the diplomatic service.

clue.text: Creature in mountain? It may be climbing below you

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece is written beneath the first

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round

explanation.surface: A question about a beast that might be scrambling up the slope beneath you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns IT upward to TI, and 'below' puts it under YE.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman is a legendary beast said to roam the Himalayas, hence the question mark.

clue.text: What gets me involved with politics as an argumentative type

indicators.note: involved means the letters are entangled together and rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking what turns someone who dabbles in politics into a quarrelsome sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who engages in polemics, writing or speaking in fierce controversy, is a combative disputant.

clue.text: Clip from the picture, a long one?

indicators.note: Clip from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A short excerpt taken from a film, perhaps a lengthy one.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, grand-scale film is called by this name, so 'a long one' means a lengthy picture.

clue.text: List of rules in old literature carried by professional officer

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the other pieces

parts.note: pro is short for professional
OT is the Old Testament, ancient scripture
Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an officer

explanation.surface: Antique writings are transported by a career army officer along with a rulebook.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal code of procedure or etiquette, as in diplomatic conventions, is a set of rules.

clue.text: Study tragic female, a lady in Italy

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Hardy's tragic heroine

explanation.surface: Scrutinise a doomed heroine, an Italian noblewoman.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Italian title for a countess, a noblewoman of that rank.

clue.text: Bobby is gloomy, needing courage

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling gloomy
bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.surface: A police officer is down in the dumps and needs to summon his nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bobby' looks like a name; it is a British policeman, and the answer is old slang for one too.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are old British slang for a police constable, a uniformed copper.

clue.text: Depressed academic hugging wife

indicators.note: hugging means the academic's letters wrap around the wife's

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A miserable university lecturer embraces his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low or in the dumps is a synonym for being depressed.

clue.text: Style of speech stars found in books

parts.note: diction is one's manner of enunciation
Aries is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: Ways of speaking and celebrities appear in the pages of novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Reference books listing words and their meanings are examples of books.

clue.text: Most recent development has the French facing ordeal

parts.note: la is French for the
a test is a trial or ordeal

explanation.surface: News just in: the French are confronting a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The latest' is the newest news or development, the most up-to-date item.

clue.text: Move in or out? I'll take everything in!

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dithering over moving house, and someone else happy to absorb anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MOVE IN OR; the definition is what the eater would say.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that eats both plants and meat consumes anything, so it might boast of eating everything.

clue.text: Brawl with no one getting charged?

definitions.meaning: read literally, nobody pays: admission is free to every person

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an uncontrolled melee, and read literally it says entry costs nothing to anybody.

clue.text: Croatian fibs? Possibly any fibs

indicators.note: possibly means the letters may be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some lies are Croatian, or whether any lies at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Invented stories and lies of any kind are falsehoods, made-up untruths.

clue.text: Debate is about what costs NHS billions

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A political argument over what drains the health budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges DEBATE IS. The NHS is Britain's state-funded National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: This chronic blood-sugar disease is a famously expensive illness for Britain's health service to treat.

clue.text: Farm animals not reared in Durham location

parts.note: livestock are farm animals

indicators.note: reared means raised up, so in a down clue the word is turned upward

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round

explanation.surface: Livestock that were not bred in County Durham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reared' turns NOT into TON. Stockton-on-Tees is a town historically in County Durham, in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The town of Stockton-on-Tees lies in County Durham, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Bury meeting said to be for mediation

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: said means we hear the word, spelt differently

parts.note: a session is a meeting

explanation.surface: A funeral gathering is reportedly held to make peace.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury here is the verb, not the Lancashire town; 'said' turns SESSION into its soundalike CESSION.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleading or intervening on someone's behalf is intervention to settle a dispute.

clue.text: After-effect of rain in Italy — letting in water maybe

parts.note: the Po is the river in Italy
after rain, a river's level rose

explanation.surface: What happens in Italy after a downpour, and something porous.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the pieces as a sentence: after rain, the Po (Italy's great river) rose.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare word meaning porous, full of tiny holes that allow liquid through.

clue.text: Organises group drink

parts.note: a set is a group
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone arranges a drink for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange or establish something is a phrasal synonym of organise.

clue.text: Milton Keynes etc. very warm? It may be bad news for game!

definitions.text: It may be bad news for game!

parts.note: Milton Keynes is a town in Bucks, short for Buckinghamshire, an English county
hot is very warm

explanation.surface: An odd remark about a hot day in Milton Keynes.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is the usual abbreviation for Buckinghamshire, the county containing Milton Keynes; game here is hunted animals, not sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse lead shot fired from a shotgun is used for hunting deer and birds, which is grim for quarry.

clue.text: Top individual criminal in America

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid
one is an individual, a single person

explanation.surface: The top crook in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster of the Prohibition era.

clue.text: Drug agent from US contributing to anarchy

indicators.note: contributing to means the answer forms part of the following word

explanation.surface: An American narcotics officer helping to cause chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for an undercover narcotics officer, a member of the drug squad.

clue.text: Archbishop's exclamation of annoyance you texted

parts.note: tut is a sound of irritation
U is how you is written in a text message

explanation.surface: A senior cleric tuts in annoyance at a text you sent.
explanation.walkthrough: Desmond Tutu was Archbishop of Cape Town.
explanation.definitionFit: Desmond Tutu, the South African Nobel laureate, was Anglican Archbishop of Cape Town.

clue.text: Decorative coverings in a capital city nabbed by criminals

indicators.note: nabbed by means caught and held inside by the criminals

parts.note: cons are convicts
Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: Fancy fabrics in a European capital are snatched by thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental cloths spread over a horse's saddle and harness are ornate trappings.

clue.text: Some pans in kitchen may be in this

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few cooking pans may be sitting in the washing-up basin.
explanation.definitionFit: The kitchen basin is where dirty pans pile up for washing, so they may well be there.

clue.text: Reprobate will have nothing to do with Dickensian character

parts.words: will have nothing to do with
parts.note: to black something is to boycott it
Uriah Heep is the scheming clerk in David Copperfield

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer shuns a Dickens figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The disgraced member of a family is a ne'er-do-well, a rogue.
